outcomes.answer_text: For IVD development in late therapeutic product development, the FDA expects that clinical evidence supporting the IVD companion diagnostic will be generated during the major efficacy trial(s) intended to support approval of the therapeutic product. Consequently, the investigational IVD(s) used in these trials should be completely specified, with analytical validation complete and meeting performance expectations. Sub-topics under this section include "Training Samples Sets versus Validation Samples Sets", "Effect of Changes to the Test Design", "IVD Bridging Studies", and "Special Protocol Assessments".

The guidance document "The Least Burdensome Provisions: Concept and Principles: Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff" was issued on February 5, 2019 (following a draft issued on December 15, 2017) and supersedes the previous guidance of the same name issued on October 4, 2002. Issued by the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) and Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER), it represents the current thinking of the FDA, is nonbinding, and does not establish any legal rights. The document provides principles and examples regarding applications of least burdensome principles to medical device regulation, such as balancing premarket and postmarket information needs, using alternative approaches, and streamlining processes.

outcomes.answer_text: The guidance document titled "Considerations for Allogeneic Pancreatic Islet Cell Products" was issued by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Food and Drug Administration, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) in September 2009. This guidance represents the FDA's current thinking on the topic and nonbinding recommendations; it does not create or confer rights or bind the FDA or the public. According to the document, although modified allogeneic islet cell products are beyond its scope, manufacturing changes resulting in significant modifications—such as encapsulation—may require additional preclinical safety and proof-of-concept studies in animal models.

outcomes.answer_text: The project "Best Assessment of Sore Throat and Antibiotic prescribing" (BASTA) aims to investigate whether altering patient flow away from medical practitioners can lower unnecessary antibiotic prescribing for patients whose primary complaint is a sore throat. Its primary objective is to determine if managing uncomplicated acute sore throat according to prevailing guidelines differs depending on whether the initial assessment is conducted by a medical practitioner, a trained nurse, or a trained pharmacist.
